args.root_cause: In `parse_orders_csv`, the very first line force-encodes the entire CSV input to ASCII, silently dropping every non-ASCII character before the CSV is parsed: `text = text.encode("ascii", errors="ignore").decode("ascii")`. Any accented letter (é, í, Å, etc.) in any field, including customer_name, is deleted outright, producing "Jos Martnez" from "José Martínez". The input is already a Python `str`, so no byte-level decoding is needed at this point; the ASCII round-trip is the sole cause of the loss. The fix is to remove that line (and handle real file bytes with the correct encoding, e.g. UTF-8, at the point where the file is read, if applicable).
